triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Same as index 0: the §122 surcharge was zeroed on entry_is_line_a/entry_is_line_b (China-301-list and aluminum exemplar flags) rather than on the source's exclusion-list and §232-covered exemptions, and the Brazil/forced-labor components applied by origin alone with no line-list membership test.

triage.verifier_justification: The §122 version[1] formula changes its exemption gate from `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b` to `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered`, while the rule's proof atoms are untouched — so the source ground is constant and only the population the exemption covers changed, which is scope, not groundedness. The cited proclamation (resolved through the pinned release) defines that population as "articles listed in paragraph 2 of Annex I ... and as enumerated in Annex II" plus "shall not apply in addition to tariffs imposed under section 232"; the pre-fix gate instead used the module's own exemplar flags, which the same file reads as reciprocal-annex/China-301-list-1 membership (`entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`, and `if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate`) and as aluminum-only metals membership (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b`). That is both over-inclusive (any §301-list line exempted, for every origin) and under-inclusive (§232 steel/copper articles not exempted), exactly the "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" the PR body describes. It is not a rename or mechanical churn: entry_is_line_a/b survive post-fix as separate live inputs, so the §122 gate now takes genuinely different caller inputs, and the PR reports 18 witness-slice cells changing value.

triage.verifier_notes: inferred from verified sibling module index 0 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Refutations tried and rejected: (1) Mechanical rename — no: `git show a9562cfd44:...ch01.yaml | grep entry_is_line_` shows entry_is_line_a (line 1907) and entry_is_line_b (1924) still driving entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded / entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded and the Brazil-IEEPA term (2367, 2523), so one conflated input was split into several independent ones. (2) Enhancement the module never claimed — no: this is a chapter-wide generated composition (schedule_statutory_stack over any hts_line), and its own §122 atoms cite "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04", neither of which is the set the old gate denoted. (3) Better-fitting kind — untraceable_branch does not fit because the exemption branch is source-grounded and its atoms are unchanged; polarity_or_logic does not fit because the or-shape is preserved. Reviewer caveats: the same commit also ADDS a new section_232_steel_component_rate and its ch01_s232_steel_heading_rate 0.50 parameter (new coverage, separate from the anchored defect — would be unrepresented_clause if scored on its own), and the Brazil-301 / forced-labor-301 rules gain list-membership gates whose inputs the summary says "default to the declared-boolean FALSE pattern", which zeroes those components pending membership tables. Also note this module file is 1 of 100 byte-identical generated chapter files in the commit, so the corpus should dedup rather than count 100 defects.
